transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-19 15:00 PDT | Duration 45m | Attendees: Alex Park, Sofia Martinez - Redwood; Liam Chen, Priya Nair, Marcus Lee, Zoe Patel - Ember Analytics

[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro I'm Alex AE at Redwood, with Sofia from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Liam Chen: doing good, thanks; excited to learn about quickstart and what the hosted offering looks like.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: awesome, great to meet you all. the plan — quick discovery, understand your stack and success criteria then figure out next steps: quickstart and demo. sound good?
[00:27] Zoe Patel: yep sounds great.
[00:30] Priya Nair: just to frame — we build customer-facing chat and summarization for enterprise customers, latency is important, and data residency for some accounts.
[00:40] Marcus Lee: and we're evaluating whether we can start on hosted and later move to dedicated or private. also security is big for us — SOC2, SSO, audit logs.
[00:52] Alex Park: totally. to be explicit, Redwood supports hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployments. many customers start on hosted with free credits to validate, then move to dedicated for predictable throughput or private for regulated data.
[01:10] Liam Chen: can you give rough numbers for time-to-first-token? like from sign-up to making a request?
[01:18] Sofia Martinez: yeah typically with our quickstart and free credits you can get first token in under 10 minutes; if you follow the tutorial we provide — SDK + API key — it's very fast. sometimes network issues or SSO provisioning adds time but on simple cases it's minutes.
[01:33] Priya Nair: what about streaming? we need incremental tokens for chat.
[01:37] Sofia Martinez: streaming is supported on the hosted API, we stream chunks; latency depends on model choice and sequence length. we have performance profiles per model in the catalog.
[01:47] Marcus Lee: on the security side — do you support SAML SSO and KMS for key management?
[01:53] Alex Park: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC for teams, and integrations with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; hosted has encryption at rest and in transit and we can discuss enterprise KMS options for Dedicated. we'll share SOC2 and security docs.
[02:08] Liam Chen: nice. can you explain the difference in cost and performance between hosted and dedicated? 
[02:15] Sofia Martinez: high level: hosted is usage-based and lower friction; good for PLG and getting users started. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput, lower per-token for heavy sustained workloads and data isolation. Private is for VPC/on-prem for strict compliance. In practice, if you have consistent high QPS and need SLOs, Dedicated is the path.
[02:35] Zoe Patel: do you have recommendations for models and quantization? we care about latency vs quality tradeoffs.
[02:41] Sofia Martinez: yes, our catalog includes verified profiles. for tight latency we suggest smaller quantized variants; we also recommend prefix/KV caching for chat to reduce compute on repeated contexts. we'll propose batching and quantization profiles in the Optimize recommendations.
[02:58] Priya Nair: what's the overhead of prefix caching? like if we have lots of unique conversations will cache help?
[03:04] Sofia Martinez: it depends; prefix caching helps when prompts share a lot of history or system messages. if each convo is unique, it's less effective. our runtime also does continuous batching which helps throughput for high concurrency.
[03:18] Marcus Lee: curious about autoscaling behavior for Dedicated — can it burst for traffic spikes?
[03:23] Alex Park: yes Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity options. you can set policies to maintain latency SLOs; if burst exceeds capacity, smart routing can fallback to hosted variants if you enable it.
[03:36] Liam Chen: we'll probably start with hosted for dev and a small pilot, then if stable move to Dedicated. question — free credits: how much and what do they cover?
[03:45] Alex Park: we give developer free credits on sign-up for the quickstart, usually enough for a few thousand tokens of exploration or a small pilot; for POCs we often extend credits when there's mutual interest. I'll include the quickstart link and exact free credits terms in the follow-up.
[03:59] Zoe Patel: what's the typical timeline to stand up a Private deployment? we've got some regulated customers.
[04:05] Sofia Martinez: Private (VPC) onboarding often takes several weeks — depends on networking and security review. On-prem is longer. For most customers the pattern is hosted -> Dedicated -> Private if required.
[04:17] Priya Nair: any gotchas about model compatibility when migrating across environments?
[04:21] Sofia Martinez: we try to keep the API and model variants consistent; some quantized builds or hardware-specific kernels may differ slightly, so we recommend pinning model versions and running evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and run regressions.
[04:36] Liam Chen: ok good. what about observability — do we get token-level cost breakout and per-route dashboards?
[04:43] Alex Park: yes Redwood Console includes token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces, and error analysis. You can also set rollout policies and automated fallbacks.
[04:54] Marcus Lee: for SOC2 and audit logs, do you provide access to raw logs or only summaries?
[04:59] Alex Park: we provide audit logs; in Dedicated/Private you have more control and can forward logs to your SIEM. I'll attach SOC2 summary and audit log examples in the follow-up.
[05:10] Zoe Patel: are there customers in finance or health you can share references for private deployments?
[05:15] Alex Park: yes, we have a couple — I'll include anonymized references.
[05:20] Priya Nair: for the pilot, we'd like to measure p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens. can Redwood help run a benchmark?
[05:27] Sofia Martinez: absolutely — SEs run perf tests with your sample prompts and we can capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput. we'll need a sample prompt set and traffic pattern.
[05:36] Liam Chen: our goal is p99 < 250ms for short chat turns, and cost ideally under $X per 1k tokens — we'll quantify.
[05:45] Alex Park: noted. also curious — are you using any embedding or reranking flows?
[05:50] Zoe Patel: embeddings for search and reranking for personalized results; separate budgets but relevant.
[05:55] Sofia Martinez: good, we support embeddings and reranking APIs and can include those in the pilot.
[06:01] Marcus Lee: ok questions from infra: do you support VPC peering and private endpoints for hosted or is that only Private?
[06:08] Alex Park: we support private endpoints for Dedicated and Private; hosted is public but you can restrict via IP allowlists and VPC peering is available for Private. We'll clarify modes in docs.
[06:20] Priya Nair: any limits on concurrency per API key?
[06:24] Sofia Martinez: hosted has default rate limits but you can request increases; Dedicated gives you predictable concurrency based on reserved GPUs.
[06:31] Liam Chen: ok, what will you send in the follow-up?
[06:34] Alex Park: pricing sheet, quickstart link, SOC2 + security docs, and a proposed timeline for demo + benchmark. Sofia will book a demo.
[06:42] Zoe Patel: sounds good.
[06:44] [Longer silence as participants review notes]
[06:58] Priya Nair: quick nit — do you have client SDKs in Python and Node?
[07:02] Sofia Martinez: yes both plus examples for streaming in Node.
[07:07] Liam Chen: do you support function/tool calling style for structured outputs?
[07:11] Sofia Martinez: yes we support function-calling and structured output helpers in the SDK.
[07:16] Marcus Lee: for the benchmark, can you run with quantized variants to see latency improvements?
[07:20] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll include quantized and non-quantized runs.
[07:24] Zoe Patel: any common transcription or model behavior regressions we should watch for when migrating?
[07:29] Sofia Martinez: regression risk exists when changing model families or quantization; Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets so you can detect regressions.
[07:39] Alex Park: okay let's recap action items and next steps.
[07:44] Alex Park: action item 1: I'll send pricing and quickstart. action 2: Sofia will schedule 1-hour demo + perf run. action 3: Ember to share sample prompts and traffic profile. anyone want to add?
[07:58] Liam Chen: Priya will own sending prompts.
[08:02] Priya Nair: yep will send by Monday.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: I'll sync with our security team and review SOC2 docs.
[08:09] Zoe Patel: thanks folks.
[08:11] Alex Park: great thanks all, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow with docs and calendar invite.
[08:16] Meeting end.
